corrections: Split seven long lessons into 38 units with stable distinct IDs, sourceLesson, honest 3–5-minute values, ordered migrations, unit-specific takeaways, and independent focused question files.

Preserved all fourteen archival MD/question files byte for byte and all 84 original question IDs, type, level, answer keys and option counts; no new question was required because every unit had at least one suitable original question.

Added explanatory code comments for field extraction, byte order, fragment alignment/offset units, reverse mappings, route matching, settled-node skipping, path relaxation, tuple ranking, DHCP option bounds/concatenation and timer output. Original native executable statements remain identical; one added ipaddress import makes the split aggregation snippet standalone.
Corrected RFC 6691 advertised-MSS versus actual-payload wording: the advertisement subtracts fixed headers without options; a sender separately reduces its actual data length for included options.

Made the sequential IPv4 Identification wrap calculation dimensionally explicit, including grouped rate denominators and every unit. Used conventional implicit algebra in products and bracketed compound expressions.

Added local prerequisite context for Python strict network parsing, documentation-only NAT64 suffix encoding, and source-specific Linux reply routing so each moved question is answerable before completion of its own unit.

Qualified the 4-to-3 modulo ECMP example with uniform-hash, removed-last-path and stable-surviving-index assumptions; removed the overstatement that changing the path count changes almost every remainder in general.

Audited every inherited glossary definition, alias and example. Corrected/qualified 180 inherited entries and retained all 430 IDs, adding three precise local terms. Review groups overlap; 180 is an entry count, not an atomic-fact claim count.

Significant glossary repairs include NAT mapping versus filtering, no inherent VPN encryption, IP scope versus actual reachability, /31 limited-broadcast distinction, non-atomic Identification semantics, OSPF flooding/adjacency/area summaries, source preference, non-universal route withdrawal, no TLS plaintext guarantee from rogue DHCP, DAD/ARP non-guarantees, and DHCP timing/configuration qualifications.
Corrected the DHCP magic-cookie definition: BOOTP can use the same RFC 1048-style cookie, so its presence alone does not distinguish DHCP from every BOOTP message.

Removed stale prevalence/default/timing guarantees from inherited examples (Linux majority, fixed keepalive interval, universal MAC rotation, guaranteed direct NAT traversal, universal SPF per event, always-fatal malformed BGP UPDATE, global ROA coverage). Replaced a provider-specific community number with an explicitly hypothetical agreed tag.

Avoided wrong dictionary senses using OSPF LSA flooding, network reply path, IPv4 option padding, BGP export restrictions, private ASN ranges, inter-AS peering, strict network parsing, AS-path validation and longest matching IP prefix. Checked the real compiled IDs, full definitions and rendered links.

Preserved genuine drawings. The count-to-infinity drawing keeps its exact topology and costs but labels costs with numbers instead of undefined d equations; SPF tables describe distance updates in words. Eleven diagrams compile and render in the author fixture.

Repaired dead glossary source URLs for renumbering, floating static routes, five-tuples, decimal prefixes, special-purpose addresses and DHCP security.
